'''Viviane Baladi''' (born 23 May 1963) is a mathematician who works as a director of research at the [[Centre national de la recherche scientifique]] (CNRS) in France. Originally Swiss, she has become a naturalized citizen of France.<ref name="cv">{{citation|url=http://webusers.imj-prg.fr/~viviane.baladi/cv.html|title=Curriculum vitae: Viviane Baladi|publisher=[[Centre national de la recherche scientifique]]|access-date=2015-10-14}}.</ref> Her research concerns [[dynamical system]]s.

==Education and career==
Baladi earned masters degrees in mathematics and computer science in 1986 from the [[University of Geneva]].<ref name="cv"/> She stayed in Geneva for her doctoral studies, finishing a Ph.D. in 1989 under the supervision of [[Jean-Pierre Eckmann]], with a dissertation concerning the [[Artin–Mazur zeta function|zeta functions of dynamical systems]].<ref>{{mathgenealogy|id=48860}}.</ref>

She worked at CNRS beginning in 1990, with a leave of absence from 1993 to 1999 when she taught at [[ETH Zurich]] and the University of Geneva. She also spent a year as a professor at the [[University of Copenhagen]] in 2012–2013.<ref name="cv"/>

==Books==
She is the author of the book ''Positive Transfer Operators and Decay of Correlation'' (Advanced Series in Nonlinear Dynamics 16, World Scientific, 2000)<ref>Review of ''Positive Transfer Operators and Decay of Correlation'' by Jérôme Buzzi (2001), {{MR|1793194}}.</ref> and of ''Dynamical Zeta Functions and Dynamical Determinants for Hyperbolic Maps: A Functional Approach'' ([[Ergebnisse der Mathematik und ihrer Grenzgebiete]] 68, Springer, 2018).<ref>Reviews of ''Dynamical Zeta Functions and Dynamical Determinants for Hyperbolic Maps'': Claudio Bonanno, {{MR|3837132}}; Kazuhiro Sakai, {{zbl|1405.37001}}</ref>

==Recognition==
She was an [[list of International Congresses of Mathematicians Plenary and Invited Speakers|invited speaker at the International Congress of Mathematicians]] in 2014, speaking in the section on "Dynamical Systems and Ordinary Differential Equations".<ref>{{citation|url=http://www.mathunion.org/db/ICM/Speakers/SortedByLastname.php|title=ICM Plenary and Invited Speakers since 1897|publisher=[[International Mathematical Union]]|access-date=2015-10-01|archive-date=2017-11-24|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171124141541/http://www.mathunion.org/db/ICM/Speakers/SortedByLastname.php|url-status=dead}}.</ref> She became a member of the [[Academia Europaea]] in 2018.<ref>{{citation|title=List of members|publisher=Academia Europaea|url=https://www.ae-info.org/ae/Acad_Main/List_of_Members|access-date=2020-10-02}}</ref>
Baladi was awarded the [[CNRS Silver Medal]] in 2019.<ref>{{citation|url=https://www.cnrs.fr/fr/talents/cnrs?medal=39|title=Médaille d'argent du CNRS|date=26 January 2023 }}</ref>
